title: Investigate field capacity: are metres of water labelled as kg/m²?
status: PROVISIONAL — do not submit as a confirmed erratum
description: The published soil-water capacity tops out at only 1.20 kg/m² for a 4.6 m soil column. That looks more like a depth of water in metres than a mass per area, suggesting a possible missing water-density conversion. This is not confirmed yet.
example: Taken literally, the biggest capacity would be only about 1.2 mm of water across the entire soil column. A drought metric dividing soil water by this capacity could be wildly inflated if the suspected ×1000 mistake is real.
scientific_evidence: All 138 fixed-file headers were inspected; numerical samples across the 15 r1 experiments have the same suspicious range, 0–1.199801 kg m⁻² for a 4.6 m soil column. A missing ×1000 water-density conversion is plausible. However, the bundled resource already has the low values and the kg m⁻² label, so the native generation step has not been independently reconstructed. Do not apply a factor from plausibility alone.
